## Problem

LIMSOC Permission Assist is a single-page vanilla-JS tool (repo `nicholas-wood/limsoc-permission-assist`) that Life Saving Victoria uses to maintain LIMSOC permission groups. It runs only as a claude.ai artifact or a local file. It embeds a snapshot of LIMSOC staging group and permission names, so it cannot be put on a public URL, and it loads its Excel library from cdnjs, which rules out a strict content security policy. It has no home behind an organisational sign-in, no deploy pipeline, and no rollback.

## Vision

Nick opens `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`, signs in exactly as he does for the Operational Service Summary, and the page he knows appears with the staging example loaded. He uploads a Groups export, ticks, downloads the import file. Nothing about the tool changed; what changed is that a signed-out request gets the sign-in page and nothing else, the browser is technically unable to call anything but its own origin, and a push to main puts a new build live with the previous one a single command away.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the app's behaviour, layout, wording or LIMSOC look beyond what hosting and security require.
- Any call to LIMSOC, production (limsoc.com.au) or staging, from the app, the gate, CI or my testing. Import testing on staging.limsoc.com.au is Nick's.
- A backend for group rules. They stay in localStorage (`lsvperm-rules`).
- A second sign-in system, load balancer, IAP, CDN, or a second Cloud Run service.
- Restructuring the Operational Service Summary app (its basePath, routes, or data model), which another session is still building.
- Analytics, error reporting or any third-party call.
- Making the repository public.

## Principles

- **One gate, one audit.** Sign-in, session and membership checks are the gate's existing code paths, not a copy.
- **Nothing readable without a session.** Page, vendored script, any other path under the prefix, and the bucket itself all refuse a signed-out request.
- **Least privilege by default.** A new app starts with one allowed person and an explicit grant per person after that.
- **The browser cannot be asked to misbehave.** The CSP forbids network calls outright, so "never talks to LIMSOC" is enforced, not promised.
- **Additive to shared things.** The gate repo and Terraform state are shared with in-flight work; changes there are new files or minimal hunks.
- **Cost honesty.** Anything outside the free tier is surfaced with an estimate before it is created.

## Constraints

- URL: `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`. The domain mapping is gated on Nick's GoDaddy nameserver change (inherited from the gate project); until then the interim host is `lsv-oss-prod-ixkidoqqka-ts.a.run.app`.
- Gate: Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`, project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Next.js 15.5.6 with `basePath: "/lsv/dailysummary"`, Firebase Auth session cookie `session` (httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days), Firestore `members` allow-list.
- Storage: one GCS bucket in `lsv-oss-prod`, Standard class, australia-southeast1, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention enforced, versioning on, no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers, no signed URLs. Only `lsv-oss-run` holds `roles/storage.objectViewer` on it.
- CI: GitHub Actions with Workload Identity Federation, no JSON keys. Push to main builds and deploys.
- Build: edit `src/`, run `python3 build.py`, never hand-edit `dist/`. xlsx pinned at 0.18.5, vendored, hash-checked.
- Headers: strict CSP (`script-src 'self'` plus the inline script hash), `Cache-Control: no-store` on HTML, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, plus the gate's nosniff, frame deny, referrer, permissions and HSTS set.
- Tooling: bun and TypeScript for new scripts; Python only for the existing `build.py`. gcloud, terraform and gh exist only on the Mac (`ssh mac`).
- Wording: "members", never "staff".

 * what the page shows as new.

import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";

type Snapshot = { kind: string; perms: [number, string][]; groups: { name: string; perms: number[] }[] };

const root = resolve(dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname), "..");
const snap = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, "data/staging-snapshot-2026-11-14.json"), "utf8")) as Snapshot;
if (snap.kind !== "limsoc-permission-snapshot") throw new Error("Not a LIMSOC permission snapshot");

const codename = new Map(snap.perms.map(([id, label]) => [id, label.split(" | ").pop()!]));
const groups = snap.groups.map((g) => ({ name: g.name, perms: g.perms.map((id) => codename.get(id)!) }));
const superuser = groups.find((g) => /^superuser$/i.test(g.name));

if (groups.some((g) => /^superuser\s*\(last run\)$/i.test(g.name))) throw new Error("Snapshot already has a last-run group");

const lastRun = { name: "Superuser (last run)", perms: [...superuser.perms] };
superuser.perms = [...new Set(codename.values())];
groups.push(lastRun);

# Deploying LIMSOC Permission Assist

Hosted at **https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist**, behind the same sign-in as the LSV Operational Service Summary.

## How it is put together

| Part | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| Site files | `index.html` and `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js` | Private bucket `gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist` (project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Standard class, versioned) |
| Gate | Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`: checks the session, checks the member's grant, then reads the bucket server-side | Repo `nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary` (`src/lib/static-app.ts`, `src/app/apps/[app]`) |
| Infrastructure | Bucket, IAM, deploy account, WIF provider | `infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf` in the gate repo |
| Pipeline | Build and check on every push; publish on `main` | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` in this repo |

The bucket has public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access. No one can read it by URL, and no signed URLs are issued. Two accounts can touch it: the gate's runtime account (`lsv-oss-run`, read only) and this repo's deploy account (`limsoc-pa-deploy`, objects in this bucket only).

The page is served with a content security policy that allows scripts from this site only, plus the page's own inline script by hash, and allows no network connections at all (`connect-src 'none'`). The browser cannot call LIMSOC or anything else from this page. HTML is `no-store` and every response is `noindex`.

## Deploy

Push to `main`. GitHub Actions rebuilds with `SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/`, checks the build, and uploads to the bucket. The gate picks up the new files on the next request; nothing is restarted.

```
git push origin main
```

Pull requests run the build and checks without publishing.

Make changes in `src/` and run `python3 build.py`; commit the rebuilt `dist/`. CI fails if `dist/` does not match a fresh build.

To publish by hand (needs `gcloud` signed in with access to the bucket):

```
SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/ python3 build.py
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js $B/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js
gcloud storage cp dist/index.html $B/index.html
python3 build.py   # put dist/ back to the committed local-file build
```

## Rollback

Every upload keeps the previous build (the bucket keeps the ten most recent versions of each file). To put the previous page back:

```
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp "$(gcloud storage ls -a $B/index.html | sort -t'#' -k2 -n | tail -2 | head -1)" $B/index.html
```

It is live on the next request. To pick a specific build, list them with `gcloud storage ls -a -l $B/index.html` and copy the one you want (`$B/index.html#<generation>`) over `$B/index.html`.

Then fix `main` (for example `git revert <commit> && git push`), or the next push will publish the same thing again.

## Adding a member

Access needs two things: the person is on the gate's member allow-list, and they hold the `limsoc-permission-assist` grant. One command does both. Run it from a checkout of the gate repo (`nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary`) on a machine where `gcloud auth application-default login` has been done:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts grant limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com "First Last"
```

They then sign in at the address above with an emailed link. Other commands:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts list   limsoc-permission-assist
bun run scripts/app-access.ts revoke limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com
```

A grant or a revoke takes effect on the person's next request. Nothing is redeployed.

Note: the allow-list is shared with the Operational Service Summary. Anyone added here is a gate member, so today they can also open `/lsv/dailysummary`. Revoking the grant removes Permission Assist only; to remove someone entirely, remove them from the allow-list in the gate.

## Monthly cost

Effectively nothing: well under 5 cents a month.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Uploads | 2 writes per deploy at $0.005 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Reads | 1 conditional read per page or script request at $0.0004 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |
| Gate | Existing Cloud Run service, scales to zero, inside its free tier at this usage | $0 extra |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## First-time setup (once)

1. Merge the gate change and apply its Terraform (`infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf`), which creates the bucket, the read binding, the deploy account and the WIF provider.
2. Deploy the gate so the route exists.
3. Grant the first member (command above).
4. Create the `production` environment in this repo's GitHub settings, then push to `main`.

## Rules

- The app never calls LIMSOC. Import testing is done by hand on staging.limsoc.com.au only, never production.
- Keep this repository private. `data/` and `test/` describe LIMSOC's permission structure.
- Do not make the bucket public, add `allUsers`, or hand out signed URLs.

# Deploying LIMSOC Permission Assist

Hosted on its own, behind its own sign-in. It follows the AccessBuddy and LSV Operational Service Summary patterns but shares nothing with either.

- Address: **https://permissions.nicholaswood.com.au** (once the DNS record below exists). Until then: **https://limsoc-pa-prod.web.app**.
- Google Cloud project: `limsoc-pa-prod`, region australia-southeast1.

## How it is put together

| Part | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| The page | `index.html` and `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js`, built by `build.py` | Private bucket `gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site` (Standard class, single region, versioned) |
| Host service | Cloud Run service `limsoc-pa-prod`: sign-in, session, member allow-list, then reads the bucket server-side | `host/` (Next.js, sign-in code ported from AccessBuddy by way of the Service Summary) |
| Sign-in | Firebase Auth emailed link; 14-day httpOnly `__session` cookie; allow-list in Firestore `members/` | project `limsoc-pa-prod` |
| Front door | Firebase Hosting site `limsoc-pa-prod`, every path rewritten to the Cloud Run service (Cloud Run domain mappings are not offered in australia-southeast1) | `infra/terraform/main.tf` |
| Infrastructure | All of the above, plus secrets, service accounts and the GitHub trust | `infra/terraform` (state in `gs://limsoc-pa-prod-tfstate`) |
| Pipelines | `site.yml` publishes the page on every push to `main`; `release-please.yml` and `deploy.yml` release the host service | `.github/workflows` |

The bucket has public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access. No one can read it by URL and no signed URLs are issued. Two accounts can touch it: the service's runtime account (`limsoc-pa-run`, read only) and the GitHub deploy account (`limsoc-pa-deploy`, objects in this bucket only).

The page is served with a content security policy that allows scripts from this site only, plus the page's own inline script by hash, and allows no network connections at all (`connect-src 'none'`). The browser cannot call LIMSOC or anything else from this page. HTML is `no-store` and every response is `noindex`.

## Deploy

**The page.** Push to `main`. GitHub Actions rebuilds it, checks it, and uploads it to the bucket. The service picks up the new files on the next request; nothing is restarted.

```
git push origin main
```

Make changes in `src/` and run `python3 build.py`; commit the rebuilt `dist/`. CI fails if `dist/` does not match a fresh build. Pull requests run the checks without publishing.

**The host service** (`host/`, rarely changes). Merge the open "release" pull request that release-please maintains. That cuts a release, builds the image and updates Cloud Run.

To publish the page by hand (needs `gcloud` signed in with access to the bucket):

```
SITE_BASE=/ python3 build.py
B=gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site
gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js $B/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js
gcloud storage cp dist/index.html $B/index.html
```

## Rollback

**The page.** Every upload keeps the previous build (the bucket keeps the ten most recent versions of each file). To put the previous page back:

```
B=gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site
gcloud storage cp "$(gcloud storage ls -a $B/index.html | sort -t'#' -k2 -n | tail -2 | head -1)" $B/index.html
```

It is live on the next request. To pick a specific build, list them with `gcloud storage ls -a -l $B/index.html` and copy the one you want (`$B/index.html#<generation>`) over `$B/index.html`. Then fix `main` (for example `git revert <commit> && git push`), or the next push will publish the same thing again.

**The host service.** Send traffic back to the previous revision:

```
gcloud run revisions list --service limsoc-pa-prod --region australia-southeast1 --project limsoc-pa-prod --limit 3
gcloud run services update-traffic limsoc-pa-prod --to-revisions <previous-revision>=100 --region australia-southeast1 --project limsoc-pa-prod
```

## Adding a member

Only people on the allow-list can sign in. From `host/`, on a machine where `gcloud auth application-default login` has been done:

```
bun run members add person@example.com "First Last"
```

They then go to the address above, enter their email, and use the link they are sent. Other commands:

```
bun run members list
bun run members remove person@example.com
bun run members add person@example.com "First Last" --admin   # may also manage members through /api/members
```

Adding takes effect at the person's next sign-in. Removing takes effect on their next request and ends their sessions. Nothing is redeployed.

## Monthly cost

Cents: under 50 US cents a month at the outside, most likely under 10.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Page storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Bucket operations | 2 writes per publish; 1 conditional read per page or script request | under $0.001 |
| Container images | Artifact Registry keeps the 3 newest images; 0.5 GB is free, then $0.10 per GB | $0 to about $0.10 |
| Cloud Run | Scales to zero; free tier is 2 million requests and 180,000 vCPU-seconds a month | $0 at this usage |
| Firestore, Firebase sign-in, Firebase Hosting, Secret Manager (1 secret), Cloud Build (first deploy only) | Inside their free tiers at this usage | $0 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## The custom domain

Firebase Hosting needs DNS records at GoDaddy for `permissions.nicholaswood.com.au`. To see exactly which:
